shared_elements: upright freestanding stone monument with rounded/irregular top
carved relief on a single principal face
frontal human figure with head, shoulders and arms indicated
elaborate headdress or headgear crowning the figure
circular disc/medallion worn on the chest
banded horizontal elements across the lower body
museum plinth and label in the display
justification: Both are tall, tapering stone slabs bearing a single frontal figure whose head with a broad headdress occupies the top, arms and a round chest disc the middle, and horizontal banding the lower zone — a genuinely comparable vertical scheme. The manner of execution is very different, however: A is heavily eroded, blocky and shallowly incised in dark coarse stone with sparse, simplified motifs, while B is crisp, deeply undercut pale stone crowded with fine curvilinear detail and serpentine forms filling every field.
